---
name: multi-cdp-browser
description: Control isolated, persistent browser environments through the multi-cdp MCP server. Use this skill whenever the user asks to browse or interact with websites, log in somewhere, inspect console/network/performance, take screenshots, test or reload browser extensions, manage browser environments, or run several browser tasks at once, even when they do not mention multi-cdp. Prefer this workflow over Playwright or a standalone Chrome DevTools server whenever multi-cdp tools are available.
compatibility: OpenCode 2.2.5 or newer with the multi-cdp MCP server configured
---

# Multi-CDP browser workflow

Every conversation gets its own browser environment: a separate profile, port and set of
tabs. The first browser call creates it; later calls reuse it. Nothing is shared between
conversations unless you hand an environment over on purpose.

## Cheat sheet

Call as `tools["multi-cdp"].<name>(args)` inside `execute`. Do not search the catalog for these.

| Tool | Args |
| --- | --- |
| `cdp_environment_create` | `{ name?, headless?, fresh?, devExtensionPaths? }` |
| `cdp_environment_list` | `{}` (shows state, owner, `extensionControl`) |
| `cdp_environment_select` | `{ environmentId }` |
| `cdp_environment_stop` | `{ environmentId? }` |
| `cdp_environment_release` | `{}` |
| `cdp_extension_list` | `{}` (check `controllable` before toggling) |
| `cdp_extension_set_enabled` | `{ extensionId, enabled }` |
| `cdp_extension_reload` | `{ extensionId }` |
| `list_pages` / `select_page` | `{}` / `{ pageId, bringToFront? }` |
| `new_page` / `navigate_page` | `{ url }` / `{ pageId, type: "url", url, timeout? }` |
| `take_snapshot` / `take_screenshot` | `{ pageId }` |
| `click` / `hover` | `{ pageId, uid \| selector \| x+y, bringToFront?, dblClick? }` |
| `fill_form` / `type_text` / `press_key` | `{ pageId, elements }` / `{ pageId, text }` / `{ pageId, key }` |
| `evaluate_script` | `{ pageId, function, timeout?, bringToFront? }` |
| `list_console_messages` / `list_network_requests` | `{ pageId }` |

## Before the first browser call

Decide what the task needs, then either let the first call create a default environment
or call `cdp_environment_create` yourself:

| Task | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Reading pages, screenshots, DOM, console, network, performance | Just call `list_pages`; the default headless environment is created for you |
| Login, CAPTCHA, extension popups, toolbar actions, anything the user must see or do | `cdp_environment_create({ headless: false })` |
| Work the user will come back to later | Add a stable `name`, for example `{ name: "shop-checkout" }` |
| A clean browser with no cookies or extensions from the template | Add `fresh: true` |
| Testing an extension build from this project or worktree | Add `devExtensionPaths: ["<absolute path to the unpacked build>"]` |

When the user has to sign in, open a visible environment, navigate to the login page and
ask them to sign in. The profile keeps that login across stop and resume.

## Working with pages

1. Get a `pageId` from `list_pages` (or `new_page`) before page-scoped calls.
2. Prefer `take_snapshot` and element `uid`s for clicking and filling forms.
3. Controls that hide on mouse-out (video players, menus) invalidate snapshot `uid`s. Use
   `hover({ pageId, selector })`, then `click({ pageId, selector })`; the pointer stays
   where `hover` left it.
4. Background tabs throttle timers and `requestAnimationFrame`. Pass `bringToFront: true`
   to `evaluate_script`, `click` or `hover` for anything timing-sensitive.
5. Keep in-page waits under about 15 s. For longer scripts pass `timeout` (ms, max 170000)
   to `evaluate_script`.
6. A navigation timeout usually means the load event was slow, not that the page failed.
   The result includes the URL and `readyState`; check them before retrying, and pass a
   larger `timeout` for heavy sites.

## Extension development

1. Build the extension first; the browser loads the unpacked directory, not your sources.
2. `cdp_extension_list` gives IDs, enabled state and `controllable`.
3. After rebuilding, call `cdp_extension_reload`.
4. Use `cdp_extension_set_enabled` for on/off tests. A disabled extension stays disabled
   across restarts until you enable it again.
5. `install_extension` only reads the OS temp directory, `devExtensionPaths` and the
   configured `backend.filesystemRoots`. Prefer `devExtensionPaths` for worktree builds.
6. Verify behaviour through page effects, console output or network activity, not only by
   checking that the extension is listed.
7. If `extensionControl` is `unavailable`, read `extensionControlError`. Google Chrome
   ignores command-line extensions; extension control needs Chromium, Brave or Edge.
   Otherwise `cdp_environment_stop` and retry.

## Reuse and handover

- Use the environment bound to this conversation unless the user asks for another one.
- Check `cdp_environment_list` before creating more named environments.
- `cdp_environment_select({ environmentId })` resumes a stopped environment or takes over
  an idle one from another conversation. Do this only when the user wants that.
- Never assume two conversations share tabs, cookies, selected pages or extension state.

## Identity

OpenCode sends the conversation's session ID with every call, including calls from
`execute`. If a call still fails with "No caller identity", pass
`callerId: "<current session ID>"` on every call, always the same value, or pass
`environmentId` to address an environment directly.

## Lifecycle

- `cdp_environment_stop` closes the browser and keeps the profile. The next browser call
  resumes it.
- `cdp_environment_release` unbinds this conversation without stopping the browser.
- Stop environments you no longer need; they hold memory and a port.

## Destructive operations

Delete only when the user explicitly asks.

- `cdp_environment_delete({ environmentId })` permanently removes one profile. Pass
  `force: true` only if the user wants a running environment stopped and deleted.
- `cdp_environment_delete_all` removes every environment. Call it only after an explicit
  delete-all request, with `confirm: "DELETE ALL ENVIRONMENTS"`.

## Reporting

Say which environment you created, selected, stopped or deleted when it matters. Never
expose cookie values, tokens, private page content, profile files or session IDs.

# multi-cdp-mcp An MCP server that gives every AI agent conversation its own persistent, isolated Chromium browser. Works with Chrome, Edge, Brave and Chromium on Windows, macOS and Linux. It wraps the official [`chrome-devtools-mcp`](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp) tools and adds environment management and extension control.

The demo shows three OpenCode sessions working in parallel, each in its own browser: one signs in to a test CRM, the second checks the same CRM at the same time and is still signed out, and the third fills a shopping cart. ```text OpenCode conversation A ─┐ ┌─ environment A ─ browser profile A (port 9400) OpenCode conversation B ─┼─ multi-cdp-mcp ─┼─ environment B ─ browser profile B (port 9401) OpenCode conversation C ─┘ └─ environment C ─ browser profile C (port 9402) ``` ## Features - **One browser per conversation.** The first browser call creates an environment for that conversation. Tabs, cookies, logins and extensions never leak between conversations. - **Persistent profiles.** Stop an environment and resume it later with its logins and extension state intact. Name environments to come back to them. - **Any Chromium browser.** Detects Chromium, Brave, Edge or Chrome automatically, or uses the binary you configure. - **Extension control.** List, enable, disable and reload any extension. Load unpacked builds per environment (`devExtensionPaths`), handy for testing worktree builds side by side. - **Headless or visible.** Headless by default; pass `headless: false` when a human has to log in or watch. - **Agent-friendly page tools.** `evaluate_script` gets an in-page `timeout`; `click` and `hover` accept a CSS `selector` or `x`/`y`; `bringToFront` avoids throttled background tabs. - **Survives crashes.** Browsers outlive the server. A restarted server reconnects to them after checking each browser's profile path. - **Agent skill included.** Teaches the agent when to use visible windows, how to test extensions and how to clean up safely. ## Requirements - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.2 or newer. - A Chromium-based browser: Chromium, Brave, Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome. Google Chrome 137+ ignores command-line extensions, so extension control and `devExtensionPaths` need Chromium, Brave or Edge. Everything else works in Chrome. - For OpenCode: version 2.2.5 or newer. Older versions do not send the conversation ID from Code Mode, so agents must pass `callerId` themselves. ## Install Add the server to your OpenCode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`, or `opencode.jsonc` in a project): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "mcp": { "servers": { "multi-cdp": { "type": "local", "command": ["bunx", "github:igorovh/multi-cdp-mcp#v0.2.1"], "codemode": true, "timeout": { "startup": 60000, "catalog": 30000, "execution": 600000 } } } } } ``` `#v0.2.1` pins a release. Change it to a newer tag to upgrade; without a tag, `bunx` may keep using whatever version it cached first. Restart OpenCode and check that it connects: ```sh opencode mcp list ``` Then install the agent skill, so agents know how to use the tools well: ```sh bunx github:igorovh/multi-cdp-mcp#v0.2.1 install-skill ``` It copies [`multi-cdp-browser`](./.opencode/skills/multi-cdp-browser/SKILL.md) to `~/.config/opencode/skills/`. Other MCP clients work the same way: run `bunx github:igorovh/multi-cdp-mcp#v0.2.1` as a stdio server.
Install from a local clone instead ```sh git clone https://github.com/igorovh/multi-cdp-mcp cd multi-cdp-mcp bun install ``` ```jsonc "command": ["bun", "run", "/path/to/multi-cdp-mcp/src/index.ts"] ```
## Configuration Everything works without a config file. To change defaults, create `config.json`: | OS | Default config path | | --- | --- | | Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\multi-cdp-mcp\config.json` | | macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/multi-cdp-mcp/config.json` | | Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/multi-cdp-mcp/config.json` (`~/.config/...`) | Set `MULTI_CDP_MCP_CONFIG` to use another file. Partial files are fine; unknown keys and wrong types stop the server with a clear error. A full example is in [`config.example.json`](./config.example.json). | Option | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `browser.executable` | `"auto"` | Path to the browser binary, or `"auto"` (tries Chromium, Brave, Edge, Chrome) | | `browser.headless` | `true` | Default for new environments; agents can override per environment | | `browser.allowSync` | `false` | Allow browser sync. Off by default, which also stops Edge from signing new profiles in to your Windows account | | `browser.extraArgs` | `[]` | Extra command-line switches for every browser | | `browser.portRange` | `9400`–`9499` | Local CDP ports, one per running environment | | `profileSource.mode` | `"fresh"` | `fresh`: empty profiles. `clone`: copy your browser profile once into a template. `template`: reuse a prepared template | | `profileSource.sourceUserDataDir` | `"auto"` | Profile to clone; `"auto"` uses the detected browser's own profile | | `extensions.devExtensionPaths` | `[]` | Unpacked extensions loaded into every environment | | `backend.filesystemRoots` | `[]` | Extra directories `install_extension` and other path tools may read | | `dataRoot` | per-OS data dir | Where profiles, templates and logs live | | `limits.maxEnvironments` | `8` | Running environments at once | More options and details: [`docs/CONFIGURATION.md`](./docs/CONFIGURATION.md). > **`clone` copies your real browser profile**, including cookies and saved sessions, > into `dataRoot`. Close the browser before the first copy. Some sites (and Chrome's > app-bound cookie encryption on Windows) still require a fresh login; sign in once inside > the environment and it stays signed in. ## Tools All `chrome-devtools-mcp` tools keep their names and results. The server adds: | Tool | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `cdp_environment_create` | Create and bind an environment (`name`, `headless`, `fresh`, `devExtensionPaths`) | | `cdp_environment_list` | List environments with state, owner and extension-control status | | `cdp_environment_select` | Resume an environment, or take over an idle one | | `cdp_environment_stop` | Close the browser, keep the profile | | `cdp_environment_release` | Unbind without stopping | | `cdp_environment_delete` | Delete one environment and its profile | | `cdp_environment_delete_all` | Delete everything (requires an exact confirmation string) | | `cdp_extension_list` | Extensions with enabled state, source and `controllable` | | `cdp_extension_set_enabled` | Enable or disable an extension | | `cdp_extension_reload` | Reload an extension | ## How it works For each environment the server launches the browser itself, with its own `--user-data-dir`, a free CDP port and the bundled control extension, then starts a dedicated `chrome-devtools-mcp` process connected to that port. Calls are routed by the conversation ID that OpenCode sends in `_meta["ai.opencode/sessionID"]`; clients that send none can pass `callerId` or `environmentId`. The CDP `Extensions` domain cannot enable or disable extensions, so a tiny bundled extension with the `management` permission does it; the server drives it over CDP. Cloned Web Store extensions are re-declared as unpacked with their original keys, so their IDs and storage survive restarts. Details: [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](./docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [`docs/RESEARCH.md`](./docs/RESEARCH.md). ## Security model This is a local developer tool. Keep in mind: - Any local process can connect to an environment's CDP port on `127.0.0.1` and control that browser, including its logged-in sessions. - Any MCP caller can pass any `callerId` or `environmentId`; the server separates conversations, it does not authenticate them. - In `clone` mode, `dataRoot` holds copies of your cookies and sessions. On macOS and Linux the server creates profile directories with mode `0700`. - Agents can add directories to `devExtensionPaths`; those become readable by `install_extension` for that environment. - Browser sync is disabled unless `browser.allowSync` is `true`. Without this, Edge signs a fresh profile in to the Windows account and syncs passwords and history both ways. ## Development ```sh bun install bun run test # unit tests bun run typecheck # strict TypeScript bun run smoke # two conversations end to end (launches real browsers) bun run smoke:crash # kill the server, reconnect to the surviving browser bun run acceptance # three concurrent conversations ``` The end-to-end scripts use `"auto"` browser detection and fresh profiles. Set `MULTI_CDP_BROWSER=` to pick a browser, or `MULTI_CDP_CLONE_FROM=` to test cloning. `MULTI_CDP_MCP_VERBOSE=1` enables debug logs on stderr. Troubleshooting: [`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`](./docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

# Architecture

## Request path

```text
MCP tools/call
  └─ caller identity (_meta session ID, callerId or environmentId)
      └─ EnvironmentManager binding
          ├─ persistent profile + atomic process lock
          ├─ detached browser process + dedicated CDP port
          ├─ CDP client + extension-control service worker
          └─ dedicated chrome-devtools-mcp stdio client
```

`evaluate_script`, `click`, `hover`, `navigate_page` and `new_page` pass through a thin
layer (`src/server/page-tools.ts`): in-page timeouts, `bringToFront`, selector and
coordinate input through CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and page state after a navigation
timeout. Every other tool is forwarded unchanged.

The server discovers downstream tool schemas with a throwaway backend pointed at an
unreachable endpoint. `chrome-devtools-mcp` connects lazily, so discovery launches no browser.

The browser binary is resolved on the first launch (`src/browser/detect.ts`), so the server
starts and lists tools even when no browser is installed.

## Concurrency

- Creation and startup are single-flight per conversation and environment.
- Ports are reserved before the browser starts, including during concurrent starts.
- Every environment has its own backend; there is no global browser lock.
- `activeCalls` prevents stop or handover while a tool call is running.
- Cancellation and timeouts reach only the affected backend call.
- Mutating calls are never replayed after a backend failure.

## Persistence and crash recovery

`environments.json` stores profile identity, not trusted live state. MCP clients often run
one server process per project, all sharing `dataRoot`, so each write takes a lock file
(`environments.json.lock`, with dead-owner detection), re-reads the file, applies only its
own change and replaces the file atomically. Profile lock files use exclusive creation and contain the server's PID.

Browsers are launched detached, so they survive a server crash. A new server reconnects
only when the browser on the recorded port reports the environment's profile directory on
`chrome://version`; it reads the browser PID from CDP `SystemInfo.getProcessInfo`. A saved
PID is never trusted on its own, and a browser whose PID cannot be confirmed is never
force-killed.

Stopping or deleting an environment whose browser is gone does not launch a new one.

## Extension control

The CDP `Extensions` domain handles unpacked extensions only and cannot enable or disable
them. The bundled control extension holds the `management` permission. The server attaches
to its MV3 service worker and calls `chrome.management` through
`Runtime.evaluate(userGesture: true)`. The attachment keeps the worker alive; if the worker
is dormant, the server opens `chrome-extension://<id>/control.html` once to wake it.

Command-line extensions need developer mode, or Chromium disables them on restart. The
server sets `extensions.ui.developer_mode` in the profile before each launch. When an
expected extension still comes up disabled (seen on Edge), it enables developer mode
through `chrome.developerPrivate` on the browser's extensions page and re-enables the
extensions it loaded, except those the caller disabled on purpose.

## Deletion safety

Profile deletion is limited to the `envs` directory under `dataRoot`. Running environments
are rejected unless `force: true`; active calls and startups are never forced. Bulk
deletion also requires the exact string `DELETE ALL ENVIRONMENTS`.

# Configuration

The server reads one JSON file. Missing fields use the defaults in `src/config.ts`. Unknown
keys, wrong types or invalid JSON stop the server with an error naming the field.

| OS | Default path |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\multi-cdp-mcp\config.json` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/multi-cdp-mcp/config.json` |
| Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/multi-cdp-mcp/config.json`, default `~/.config/multi-cdp-mcp/config.json` |

`MULTI_CDP_MCP_CONFIG` overrides the path. In OpenCode, set it in the server's
`environment` block.

## Browser

```json
{
  "browser": {
    "executable": "auto",
    "headless": true,
    "allowSync": false,
    "extraArgs": [],
    "portRange": { "start": 9400, "end": 9499 }
  }
}
```

- `executable`: `"auto"` or a path to the browser binary. `"auto"` tries, in order:

  | Browser | Windows | macOS | Linux (`PATH`) |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Chromium | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Chromium\Application\chrome.exe` | `Chromium.app` | `chromium`, `chromium-browser` |
  | Brave | `...\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\Application\brave.exe` | `Brave Browser.app` | `brave-browser`, `brave` |
  | Edge | `...\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe` | `Microsoft Edge.app` | `microsoft-edge`, `microsoft-edge-stable` |
  | Chrome | `...\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe` | `Google Chrome.app` | `google-chrome`, `google-chrome-stable` |

  On Windows it checks Program Files, Program Files (x86) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%`; on macOS
  `/Applications` and `~/Applications`. Google Chrome is last because Chrome 137+ ignores
  `--load-extension`: extension control and dev builds need another browser.
- `headless`: default for new environments. Agents override it with
  `cdp_environment_create({ headless: false })`; the choice is stored with the profile.
- `allowSync`: `false` (default) adds `--disable-sync`, and on Edge disables
  `msImplicitSignin`. Without it, Edge signs every fresh profile in to the Windows account
  and turns sync on, so the agent's profile would receive your passwords and history.
- `extraArgs`: extra switches for every launch, for example `["--lang=en-US"]`. Your own
  `--disable-features=...` values are merged with the server's, not replaced.
- `portRange`: inclusive range of local CDP ports. One port per running environment.

The old top-level `braveExecutable` key was removed. Use `browser.executable`.

## Profiles

```json
{
  "profileSource": {
    "mode": "fresh",
    "sourceUserDataDir": "auto",
    "refreshTemplate": false,
    "maxTemplateSizeGb": 5
  }
}
```

- `fresh` (default): every environment starts with an empty profile.
- `clone`: copy `sourceUserDataDir` once into `<dataRoot>/templates/default`, then seed
  each new environment from that template. `"auto"` uses the detected browser's own
  user-data directory (for example `~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser`). Close that
  browser before the first copy or a refresh: a live profile is not a consistent snapshot.
- `template`: require an already prepared `<dataRoot>/templates/default`.

`refreshTemplate: true` rebuilds the template on the next server start. It affects only
future environments; existing profiles are never overwritten. `maxTemplateSizeGb` guards
against copying a huge profile by accident. Caches, crash dumps and lock files are skipped.

Cloned logins do not always survive: many sites bind sessions to the original profile,
and Chrome on Windows encrypts cookies per installation. Sign in once inside the
environment; the profile keeps it.

`cdp_environment_create({ fresh: true })` creates a one-off empty profile in any mode.

## Data directory

`dataRoot` holds `envs/<id>` (profiles), `templates/`, `logs/`, `artifacts/` and
`environments.json`.

| OS | Default `dataRoot` |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\multi-cdp-mcp` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/multi-cdp-mcp` |
| Linux | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/multi-cdp-mcp`, default `~/.local/share/multi-cdp-mcp` |

## Extensions

```json
{
  "extensions": {
    "controlExtensionPath": "<bundled>",
    "devExtensionPaths": ["/home/me/my-extension/dist"],
    "materializeProfileExtensions": true
  }
}
```

- `devExtensionPaths`: unpacked builds loaded into every environment. Each must be an
  absolute directory with a `manifest.json` and no comma in the path. Agents can add more
  per environment with `cdp_environment_create({ devExtensionPaths })`. A dev build whose
  manifest `name` matches a "Load unpacked" extension from the template replaces it.
- `materializeProfileExtensions`: keep `true` for cloned profiles. Chromium drops copied
  Web Store install records after the first launch; the server reloads those extensions as
  unpacked with their original keys, so their IDs and storage stay the same.
- `controlExtensionPath`: the bundled extension that provides enable/disable. Change it
  only for development.

Before each launch the server turns on developer mode in the profile, so the browser does
not disable command-line extensions on restart. If Edge still comes up with them disabled,
the server re-enables them from `edge://extensions`. Extensions disabled on purpose with
`cdp_extension_set_enabled` stay disabled.

## Paths readable by `install_extension`

`chrome-devtools-mcp` path tools only read inside their roots. Each environment gets:

1. `<dataRoot>/artifacts/<environment-id>`;
2. the OS temp directory;
3. `extensions.devExtensionPaths` and the environment's own `devExtensionPaths`;
4. `backend.filesystemRoots`.

Paths are compared after resolving symlinks and junctions; add the real target if a link
points elsewhere.

## Backend

```json
{
  "backend": {
    "runtime": "<the runtime running this server>",
    "enableExtensionTools": true,
    "filesystemRoots": [],
    "compactToolSchemas": true
  }
}
```

`runtime` defaults to the Bun binary that runs the server, so it works when the MCP client
starts with a minimal `PATH` (common for macOS GUI apps). `compactToolSchemas` shortens
downstream tool descriptions to their first sentence to save tokens.

## Limits

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxEnvironments` | `8` | Starting or running environments at once; stopped ones do not count |
| `startupTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Time for a browser to expose its CDP endpoint |
| `toolTimeoutMs` | `150000` | Every server-to-backend call; stays below Puppeteer's fixed 180 s protocol timeout |
| `navigationTimeoutMs` | `30000` | `navigate_page` / `new_page` timeout when the caller passes none |

`evaluate_script` also gets an in-page limit: its `timeout` argument, default
`toolTimeoutMs - 20 s`, at most 170 s.

## Caller identity

The server runs over stdio, so the request is the only place an identity can come from.
Precedence:

1. `_meta["ai.opencode/sessionID"]` (OpenCode 2.2.5+), then `_meta.sessionID`,
   `_meta.sessionId`, `_meta["opencode/sessionID"]`;
2. the `callerId` argument;
3. the transport session ID (session-aware transports only);
4. `explicit:<environmentId>` when only `environmentId` is passed, or `explicit:<name>`
   for `cdp_environment_create` with a `name`.

`cdp_environment_list` needs no identity. Calls with only an `environmentId` reach that
environment without changing its owner. `cdp_environment_stop` with an explicit
`environmentId` works for any idle environment; deleting someone else's environment needs
a takeover with `cdp_environment_select` first.

## Logging

Diagnostics go to stderr; stdout carries MCP frames. `MULTI_CDP_MCP_VERBOSE=1` adds debug
messages. Browser and backend logs are in `<dataRoot>/logs`.

# Research notes

Why the server works the way it does. Measured on Chromium 153–156 builds of Brave, Edge
and Chrome with `chrome-devtools-mcp` 1.9–1.12.

## Cloned profiles work

Copying a browser's user-data directory and launching the browser against the copy works.
Several clones run at once on separate ports and processes. Singleton locks
(`SingletonLock`, `SingletonCookie`, `SingletonSocket`) are symlinks and are not copied;
caches and crash dumps are skipped too.

## Cloned Web Store extensions vanish on the second launch

On the first launch of a clone, extensions run normally. During that session Chromium
rejects the copied preference MACs in `Default/Secure Preferences` and clears the install
records. On the next launch only command-line extensions remain.

The fix: `Secure Preferences` stores each extension's manifest including its `key` (the
public key the ID is derived from). Writing the key into the on-disk `manifest.json` and
loading the directory with `--load-extension` keeps the original ID, so
`chrome-extension://<id>/` storage survives. After the first launch Chromium drops the
stored manifest, so later launches find the extensions by scanning `Default/Extensions` for
manifests whose `key` reproduces the directory ID (`src/profile/extensions.ts`).

"Load unpacked" extensions from the source profile are cloned with an untrusted record:
Chromium keeps them disabled and refuses to enable them. Loading the same directory with
`--load-extension` makes them controllable.

Side effects: these extensions no longer auto-update, and they report
`installType: "development"`.

## Enable and disable need chrome.management

The CDP `Extensions` domain is unpacked-only and has no enable/disable command. A bundled
extension with the `management` permission fills the gap. `Runtime.evaluate` with
`userGesture: true` satisfies `chrome.management.setEnabled` without a dialog.

## The server launches the browser itself

Extension tools behave the same whether `chrome-devtools-mcp` launches the browser or
connects with `--browserUrl`. Launching it ourselves gives control over the profile
directory, port, flags and lifetime, and is the only way to pass `--load-extension`.

## Browser differences

- Google Chrome 137+ ignores `--load-extension` ("not allowed in Google Chrome"). Chromium,
  Brave and Edge accept it.
- Chromium 134+ disables command-line extensions on restart while developer mode is off;
  Edge does so after some restarts even when it was on. Hence the developer-mode
  preference and the `developerPrivate` repair.
- With a fixed `--remote-debugging-port`, Chrome and Edge do not write `DevToolsActivePort`.
  Reconnection therefore reads the profile path from `chrome://version` instead.

## Process notes

- Children spawned by Bun die with the parent, so the browser starts `detached`.
- On Windows `taskkill` without `/F` closes windows but not the browser process. A clean
  shutdown uses CDP `Browser.close`, which also flushes the profile.

## Logins

Sessions copied with a profile are often not valid: sites bind them to the original
profile, and Chrome on Windows uses app-bound cookie encryption. Signing in once inside a
persistent environment works, and stop/resume keeps it.

# Troubleshooting

## The server does not start or does not show up

```sh
opencode mcp list
```

Run the configured command by hand (for example `bunx github:igorovh/multi-cdp-mcp#v0.2.1`). Stderr
shows the reason: an invalid `config.json` names the bad field, and `braveExecutable`
must be renamed to `browser.executable`. Restart OpenCode after changing MCP configuration.

## "No Chromium-based browser found"

Install Chromium, Brave, Edge or Chrome, or set `browser.executable` to the binary. On
Linux the browser must be on `PATH`; Snap and Flatpak builds may need the full path of the
real binary.

## "No caller identity"

The client sent no session ID in `_meta`. OpenCode 2.2.5+ always sends one. For other
clients, pass `callerId: "<session ID>"` on every call, or `environmentId` to address an
environment directly.

## "Environment ... belongs to caller ..."

Another identity owns the environment, for example it was created with `callerId` and
later stopped without it. The error names the owner. Repeat the call with that `callerId`,
or pass `environmentId` to `cdp_environment_stop`. Deleting requires a takeover with
`cdp_environment_select` first.

## Template copy fails or cloned logins are missing

Close the source browser completely before the first copy or before setting
`refreshTemplate: true`. Many sites and Chrome's cookie encryption bind sessions to the
original profile: sign in once inside the environment; stop and resume keep it.

## Extension control is unavailable

`cdp_environment_list` shows `extensionControl` and `extensionControlError`.

- **Google Chrome**: Chrome 137+ ignores `--load-extension`. Use Chromium, Brave or Edge for
  extension work.
- **Other browsers**: the server retries on every extension call and wakes a dormant control
  worker. If it still fails, check `extensions.controlExtensionPath`, read
  `<dataRoot>/logs/browser-<port>.log`, then `cdp_environment_stop` and retry. A browser
  recovered after a server crash keeps the flags it was started with.

## Extensions are disabled after a restart

The server enables developer mode before every launch and re-enables extensions it loaded.
Extensions you disabled with `cdp_extension_set_enabled` stay disabled; enable them again
explicitly. Keep `extensions.materializeProfileExtensions: true` for cloned profiles, and
do not delete `Default/Extensions` inside a profile.

## "cannot be modified by user"

Chromium locks extensions whose cloned install record it does not trust. Load the
extension's directory through `devExtensionPaths` in a new environment.
`cdp_extension_list` marks such extensions `controllable: false` with a `lockedReason`.

## `install_extension` says "Access denied"

The backend only reads inside its roots: the OS temp directory, `devExtensionPaths` and
`backend.filesystemRoots`. See [`CONFIGURATION.md`](./CONFIGURATION.md).

## Timeouts and background tabs

Hidden tabs throttle timers and `requestAnimationFrame`. Pass `bringToFront: true` to
`evaluate_script`, `click` or `hover`, and keep in-page waits short. A navigation timeout
returns the page's URL and `readyState`; the page has usually loaded.

## Environment is locked

A running server owns that profile. Do not delete the lock or open the profile directory
in another browser. After a crash, the next server proves the recorded PID is dead and
takes over the stale lock.

## Port is unavailable

Widen `browser.portRange` or stop whatever uses the port. The server never attaches to an
unknown browser just because it answers on a saved port.

## Collect diagnostics

Set `MULTI_CDP_MCP_VERBOSE=1`, reproduce once, then check:

- `<dataRoot>/logs/browser-<port>.log`
- `<dataRoot>/logs/backend-<environment>.log`
- the MCP client's own log (OpenCode: `~/.local/share/opencode/log/`)

Do not share cookies, authorization headers, profile files or private screenshots.
